In this assignment, you'll be picking up where you left off with the M&Ms activity. You'll load the data and perform some basic statistical analysis. Follow the steps below to complete the assignment.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```



### Task 2: Load the M&Ms dataset from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv
```{r}
mandm <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv")
```



### Task 3: Sample 5 rows of data from the dataset
```{r}
set.seed(67)
sample_5 <- mandm |> sample_n(5)
```



### Task 4: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the sample, using either the red or black number of M&Ms
```{r}
sample_5 |>
  summarise(
    mean_black = mean(black),
    sd_black = sd(black)
  )
```



### Task 5: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the population, using the same measure as in Task 4
```{r}
mandm |>
  summarise(
    mean_black = mean(black),
    sd_black = sd(black)
  )
```



### Task 6: Compare the sample and population statistics

Compare the two sets of means and standard deviations. Are they similar?

The mean of the entire population was 73.3 and the standard deviation was 15.7. Meanwhile, the mean of the sample of five was 66.6 and the standard deviation was 18.0. The two measures were not entirely far off, but were also not very similar. The mean of the sample was nearly 7 M&Ms away from the mean of the entire population.

### Task 7: Describe the results

Write a few sentences about what you found in the data. What does this tell you about the M&Ms dataset and about the act of random sampling?

The mean of the entire population for black M&Ms was 73.3. The amount of a specific color of M&Ms varied between the various entries, which speaks to the importance of random sampling. The sample of 5 that I took was nearly seven points away from the mean. That reinforces the notion that if you take more samples, you will get more accurate statistics. The more data you collect from more random samples, the closer you will get to an accurate representation of the data you are representing.
